reviews.title: Awesome System, One Flaw Please Fix
reviews.text: I absolutely love my Eero and the way in which it constantly protects against internet threats. It even reports on these threats. Here’s where the flaw is - you can’t identify where on your devices these are coming from. PLEASE IMPLEMENT A REAL TIME TEXT OR ALERT WHEN THE SYSTEM IDENTIFIES A THREAT AND WHAT DEVICE THE THREAT IS COMING FROM SO USERS CAN SELF IDENTIFY AND STOP THESE AS THEY HAPPEN. It’s impossible to look at the activity area and identify what you were doing at the time the issue occurred. If these were alerted real time, users could at least possibly figure out where the threat is coming from. If Eero would do this, the system would be perfect and I would raise my review to 5 stars.

reviews.title: Just got eero through t-mobile and its a rip off
reviews.text:
Eero charges a premium subscription for Dynamic DNS, which is a standard feature on countless routers. The moment I discovered that, I immediately got rid of my Eero in favor of literally any other router. I will never buy a Eero product, and I will never recommend one to anyone. Eero is absolute junk.

I looked up how much this mesh system costs: $600. A $600 router, and they still lock Dynamic DNS behind a paid subscription. That is absolutely ridiculous.

Before you go to the store and buy one of these, think twice. You can buy a Netgear, TP-Link, Asus, or Google router for less money, and all of them give you far more customization without requiring a subscription. I know for a fact that with Netgear and TP-Link you can configure VPNs, firewalls, Dynamic DNS, and countless other advanced settings without being nickel-and-dimed. They’re cheaper, offer more features, give customers more control, and are simply better products.

And why does a router even need an identity protection subscription? That’s just another pointless add-on. If they aren’t paywalling firewall functionality, then the firewall should already be providing the protection most people actually need.

As you can probably tell from this review, I’m genuinely appalled by the decision to lock very basic networking features behind a subscription.

To make matters worse, I also discovered this router is app-only. You can’t even manage it through a web browser like virtually every other router on the market. Onc

reviews.title: $99 Paywall blocks important features
reviews.text:
Without the costly subscription, data usage is only viewable for static one week blocks; you cannot compare your usage week to week, nor month to month. To overcome the usage blackouts, constant screenshotting is a super annoying workaround. Saturday’s data usage disappears every Sunday, so if your ISP shows a huge spike in data and you didn’t take a screenshot at 11:59pm Sat, you’ve no proof/argument to show your ISP when you’re billed for overages.
And in the past year, those weekly usage bar graphs have become unusable—75GB usage on Tues appears the same bar as 12GB on Mon.
Speed tests used to be logged and saved automatically so you could easily view the previous 3-5 tests. That feature is also now locked behind paywall.

reviews.text: The Eero Home Device has only two Ethernet ports, which shouldn’t be that big of a deal but the system does not support IP defragmentation which means that the modem supplied by US Cellular (which only submits a wired signal goes into the Titan device and then wires the internet to the Eero thus providing WiFi. Here is some of the issues however, your a phone and the Eero app are tied together, if I don’t keep my phone on the Eero network it sometimes does not work properly. You are very limited in the capabilities of this system. I actually get faster more reliable internet from the hotspot of my Iphkne as opposed to WiFi or wired internet gameplay in my PS4. The whole reason I purchased this kit was for protected wired stable internet. Because of the cellular connection based on priority, I cannot adjust the output of the WAN connection, the maximum that I have ever gotten is 124 MBPS. This is a 1 Gig setup mind you. I have had my whole system replaced before and it’s expensive, nearly 100 dollars a month due to proprietary equipment. I’m getting fiber internet tomorrow. My century link 10 years ago was 3.5 and I could play online games with it for 35 dollars a month. I do not recommend
